verses.text: Before he died, Moses, the man of God, gave the Israelites this blessing.
He said, “The LORD came from Sinai and rose over them from Seir. He shone out from Mount Paran. He came from among tens of thousands of holy ones, with a fiery law for his people at his right hand.
Yes, he loves his people. All his holy ones are in your hand. They sit at your feet, each taking in your words.
Moses gave us the law as an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
He was king in Jeshurun when the people's leaders gathered and all Israel's tribes came together.
Let Reuben live and escape death. May his people be many.”
For Judah he said, “LORD, hear Judah's voice and bring him back to his people. He has fought for himself with his own hands. Help him against his enemies.”
About Levi he said, “Your Thummim and Urim belong to your faithful one, whom you tested at Massah and challenged at the waters of Meribah.
He said of his father and mother, ‘I haven't seen them.’ He didn't acknowledge his brothers or recognize even his own children, because the Levites followed your word and kept your covenant.
They'll teach Jacob your rulings and Israel your law. They'll burn incense before you and put whole burnt offerings on your altar.
LORD, bless his abilities and accept what his hands do. Strike down those who rise against him and those who hate him. May they never get up again.”
About Benjamin he said, “The LORD's beloved will live safely beside him. The LORD shelters him all day long, and Benjamin rests between his shoulders.”
About Joseph he said, “The LORD has blessed his land with the best gifts from the sky, with dew and with water from the depths below,
with the finest crops the sun ripens and the best that comes with each moon,
with the best of the ancient mountains and the treasures of the everlasting hills,
with the best of the earth and all it holds, and with the favor of the one who lived in the bush. May all this rest on Joseph's head, on the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.

His firstborn bull has majesty, and his horns are like the horns of a wild ox. With them he'll drive the peoples to the ends of the earth. These are Ephraim's tens of thousands and Manasseh's thousands.”
About Zebulun he said, “Celebrate when you go out, Zebulun, and when you're in your tents, Issachar.
They'll call the peoples to the mountain and offer sacrifices there in righteousness. They'll draw on all the sea provides and the treasures hidden in the sand.”
About Gad he said, “Blessed is the one who gives Gad more room. Gad lives like a lioness, tearing arm and scalp.
He chose the first share for himself, since the lawgiver's portion was reserved for him. He came with the leaders of the people and carried out the LORD's justice and his rulings with Israel.”
About Dan he said, “Dan is a lion cub leaping out of Bashan.”
About Naphtali he said, “Naphtali, you have all the favor you could ask for and are full of the LORD's blessing. Take possession of the west and the south.”
About Asher he said, “Asher is blessed with children. May his brothers welcome him, and may he dip his foot in oil.
Your gate bars will be iron and bronze, and your strength will last as long as you live.
Jeshurun, nobody is like God. He rides through the heavens to help you and across the skies in his majesty.
The eternal God is your home, and his everlasting arms are underneath you. He drove the enemy out before you and said, ‘Destroy them!’
Israel lives in safety, and Jacob's spring flows undisturbed in a land of grain and new wine. Even the sky sends down dew.
How blessed you are, Israel! Who's like you, a people rescued by the LORD? He's your shield and your triumphant sword. Your enemies will submit to you, and you'll tread on their high places.”
